subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Islam Beliefs Crime Punishment Living The Muslim Life Peace Conflict Spec A
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why might a religious believer argue that revenge does not bring true peace?
options: Because revenge tends to continue cycles of violence rather than ending them
Because revenge is required by all faiths
questions.explain: Many believers teach that revenge perpetuates conflict, whereas forgiveness can break the cycle of violence.

questions.q: Muslims describe Allah as 'transcendent', meaning that God is:
options: Beyond and above his creation, not part of it
questions.explain: Transcendence means God is beyond and above creation, not contained within the material world.

questions.q: Why is forgiveness important in many religious responses to conflict?
options: It can break cycles of revenge and allow reconciliation
questions.explain: Forgiveness is taught as a way to end cycles of revenge and rebuild relationships.

questions.q: Which non-religious group is well known for its commitment to pacifism?
options: Secular peace campaigners and groups such as CND
questions.explain: Many non-religious people are pacifists; secular groups such as CND (the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament) campaign for peace on humanist/ethical rather than religious grounds.

questions.q: What is 'pacifism'?
options: The belief that violence and war are never justified
The belief that war is always right
questions.explain: Pacifism is the principled rejection of violence and war as a means of resolving conflict.

questions.q: Malaikah in Islam are:
options: Angels who serve and obey God
questions.explain: Malaikah are angels, beings created by God who carry out his commands, such as Jibril.

questions.q: In Sunni Islam, the six articles of faith include belief in:
options: God, angels, holy books, prophets, the Last Day and predestination
questions.explain: The Sunni six articles are belief in God, angels, holy books, prophets, the Last Day and predestination.

questions.q: In Islam, Muhammad is regarded as:
options: The final prophet (the Seal of the Prophets)
questions.explain: Muslims believe Muhammad is the last and final prophet, the Seal of the Prophets.

questions.q: The angel who revealed the Qur'an to Muhammad is named:
questions.explain: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.q: Akhirah in Islam means:
questions.explain: Akhirah is the belief in life after death and an eternal existence beyond this life.

questions.q: Belief in Tawhid means Muslims reject:
options: Associating any partners or equals with God (shirk)
questions.explain: Because God is one, Muslims reject shirk, the sin of associating partners with God.

questions.q: What is meant by 'reconciliation' after conflict?
options: Restoring friendly relations between former enemies
questions.explain: Reconciliation means rebuilding relationships and trust between those who were in conflict.

questions.q: The 99 Names of Allah, such as Al-Rahman (the Merciful), help Muslims to:
options: Understand and reflect on the qualities of God
Mark the festivals of the year
questions.explain: The 99 Names describe God's attributes, helping Muslims reflect on his nature and character.

questions.q: Belief in Tawhid is reflected in Surah al-Ikhlas, which stresses that God is:
options: One, with no partner and nothing comparable to him
A father with a divine son
questions.explain: Surah al-Ikhlas declares the absolute oneness of God, stating there is nothing comparable to him.

questions.q: A common misconception about pacifism is that:
options: Many pacifists actively work for peace through non-violent means
Pacifists must be passive and do nothing about injustice
questions.explain: Many pacifists are very active, using non-violent protest and campaigning rather than doing nothing.

questions.q: Tawhid, the most important belief in Islam, means:
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness and unity of God (Allah).

questions.q: On the Day of Judgement, Muslims believe people will be:
options: Judged by God on their deeds and sent to Paradise or Hell
questions.explain: Muslims believe God will judge each person by their actions, leading to Paradise or Hell.

questions.q: The main cause of the Sunni-Shia split was disagreement over:
options: Who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad's death
questions.explain: The split arose over who should be the rightful leader of Muslims after Muhammad died.

questions.q: What is the relationship between most major religions and terrorism?
options: Mainstream religious teaching condemns terrorism and the killing of innocents
questions.explain: Mainstream religious teaching condemns terrorism, which targets innocent people.

questions.q: Which of the following is a condition of Just War theory?
options: The war must aim to destroy as many people as possible
The war must be started for personal profit
The war must be a last resort with a just cause
questions.explain: Just War theory requires a just cause, proper authority, last resort and proportionate, discriminating force.

questions.q: What is the role of 'justice' in achieving lasting peace?
options: Addressing the unfairness and grievances that can cause conflict
questions.explain: Many argue that true peace requires justice, since unresolved unfairness can lead to further conflict.

questions.q: Why do many religious believers oppose weapons of mass destruction?
options: Because they cause indiscriminate harm to civilians, breaching Just War principles
questions.explain: WMDs harm civilians indiscriminately, conflicting with the just-war principle of discrimination.
